details.text: Start at [Four-Bar Percussion, Bass and Chord Example](#small-hours). Follow its Before you start instructions and recipes in order. This is an independent project; save your course piece before trying it.

details.title: Example Scope
details.text: The recipes give the exact settings of the recorded example, so you can reproduce it. The recording is the authored version only: other values you try are not part of it. Listen to the recording first if you want a target for each channel.

details.title: Recorded Example: Rhythm, bass and a changing chord
details.text:
Four bars at 90 BPM.

Channel 1, Oilcan 1, velocity 38: in every bar MIDI 36 on steps 1 and 9, MIDI 38 on steps 4 and 12 and MIDI 37 on steps 5 and 13.

Channel 2, Polyperc 1, velocity 42: in every bar MIDI 48 on steps 1, 5 and 13 and MIDI 55 on step 9.

Channel 3, Doubledecker, velocity 26, three steps long, Chd1 3rd and Chd2 5th: in bars 1 to 3 the chord roots are MIDI 60 on step 1 and MIDI 62 on step 9 of the bar. In bar 4 they are MIDI 67 on step 49 and MIDI 60 on step 57.

Play the loop and listen for the chord at the start of bar 4: the drums and bass are unchanged, while the chords move from C and D to G and C.

recipes.title: Percussion Channel
recipes.text:
Starting point: the three settings under Before you start are done (90 BPM, steps 1-64, Snap note masks to scale Off) and channel 1 is empty. The steps below build a six-hit drum bar and repeat it in all four bars.

1. Select channel 1 (1,1). Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device, press K3, turn E3 to Oilcan 1 and press K3 to assign it. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then tap pattern slot (1,2) to assign Pattern 1 to channel 1.

2. Open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). With no step held, turn E2 to Note and turn E3 to MIDI 36 (C1). Turn E2 to Vel and set 38. Turn E2 to Len and set ½ step. Every trig you add now plays MIDI 36 at velocity 38 for half a step. In the default Oilcan kit MIDI 36, 37 and 38 trigger three different drum timbres.

3. In bar 1 (steps 1-16), hold K1 and tap steps 1, 4, 5, 9, 12 and 13. Six trigs light on the grid.

4. Turn E2 back to Note. Hold step 4 and turn E3 to MIDI 38 (D1), then release. Do the same for step 12. Hold step 5 and turn E3 to MIDI 37 (C#1), then release, and do the same for step 13. Steps 1 and 9 keep the default MIDI 36.

5. Listen: press Play and hear bar 1, then three silent bars because bars 2–4 are still empty. In bar 1, MIDI 36 falls on beats 1 and 3, MIDI 37 on beats 2 and 4, and each MIDI 38 hit sounds one step before a MIDI 37 hit. Press Stop.

6. Repeat steps 3 and 4 in each of the other three bars, using the full grid: steps 17–32 are row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. Masks and Pattern Trig do not page. Each pair below is a step number and its MIDI note:
Bar 2: 17/36, 20/38, 21/37, 25/36, 28/38, 29/37.
Bar 3: 33/36, 36/38, 37/37, 41/36, 44/38, 45/37.
Bar 4: 49/36, 52/38, 53/37, 57/36, 60/38, 61/37.

The channel now has 24 trigs in a repeating one-bar (four-beat) drum figure. Press Play and listen before you continue: the same bar repeats four times. Press Stop.

recipes.title: Bass Channel
recipes.text:
Starting point: channel 1 plays the drums and channel 2 is empty. Masks work as in the percussion recipe: E2 chooses the value, E3 sets it, and holding a step gives that step its own value.

1. Select channel 2 (2,1). Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device, press K3, turn E3 to Polyperc 1 and press K3 to assign it. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 2 on row 1, then tap pattern slot (2,2) to assign Pattern 2 to channel 2.

2. Open Masks. With no step held, turn E2 to Note and set MIDI 48 (C2), turn E2 to Vel and set 42, and turn E2 to Len and set ½ step.

3. In bar 1, hold K1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13.

4. Select Note with E2, hold step 9 and turn E3 to MIDI 55 (G2), then release. Steps 1, 5 and 13 keep the default MIDI 48.

5. Listen: press Play. In bar 1, the bass plays C2 on beats 1, 2 and 4 and G2 on beat 3 under the bar-1 drums; bars 2–4 remain silent until you enter them. Press Stop.

6. Repeat steps 3 and 4 in bars 2 to 4, adding 16 to each step number of bar 1. Each trig list is followed by the step that takes MIDI 55:
Bar 2: trigs on 17, 21, 25, 29; 25 is MIDI 55.
Bar 3: trigs on 33, 37, 41, 45; 41 is MIDI 55.
Bar 4: trigs on 49, 53, 57, 61; 57 is MIDI 55.

Listen for the pitch pattern C, C, G, C repeating once per bar under the drums.

recipes.title: Chord Channel
recipes.text:
Starting point: channels 1 and 2 play the drums and bass; channel 3 is empty. Use Doubledecker for the chord because it plays several notes at once. On Masks and Pattern Trig, all 64 steps are visible together: row 4 is steps 1–16, row 5 is 17–32, row 6 is 33–48 and row 7 is 49–64; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. These screens do not page. Pattern Note and Velocity use 16-step pages. Hold K1 and tap to add or remove a trig; hold a step and turn E3 to give it its own value.

1. Select channel 3 (3,1). Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device, press K3, turn E3 to Doubledecker and press K3 to assign it. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 3 on row 1, then tap pattern slot (3,2) to assign Pattern 3 to channel 3.

2. Open Masks. With no step held, set Note to MIDI 60 (C3), Vel to 26 and Len to 3 steps. Select Chd1 and set 3rd; select Chd2 and set 5th. Every chord now plays the root plus the notes a third and a fifth above it in the scale.

3. In bar 1, hold K1 and tap steps 1 and 9. Select Note, hold step 9 and turn E3 to MIDI 62 (D3), then release. Step 1 keeps the default MIDI 60. Press Play: in bar 1 the chord alternates C-E-G and D-F-A, two chords a bar, quietly above the bass; bars 2–4 remain silent until you enter them. Press Stop.

4. Bar 2: add trigs on steps 17 and 25.

5. Set step 25 to MIDI 62 as in step 3.

6. Bar 3: add trigs on steps 33 and 41.

7. Set step 41 to MIDI 62.

8. Bar 4: hold K1 and tap steps 49 and 57.

9. Hold step 49 and set Note to MIDI 67 (G3). Step 57 keeps the default MIDI 60.

10. Result check: listen to the whole four bars: press Play and wait for bar 4. The drums and bass repeat unchanged, but the chords move to G-B-D and then back to C-E-G. The chord intervals follow the C-major scale, so the 3rd above D is F and the 3rd above G is B. Press Stop.

title: Adding a Ghost Note
summary: Compare two bars of main hits with two bars that add a quiet hit before an accent.
prose:
Compare two ways of playing the same four-beat drum figure on Oilcan 1. Bars 1 and 2 contain only the main hits (MIDI 36 on steps 1 and 9, MIDI 37 on steps 5 and 13, all at velocity 90). Bars 3 and 4 add one quiet hit, MIDI 38 at velocity 35, on step 12 of the bar, just before the accent on step 13. This is a ghost note: a soft hit that adds movement without changing the main hits.

Settings: 90 BPM, Rate /1 (the default, one step is a sixteenth note), range 1–64 and length ½ step on all notes. Play "Adding a Ghost Note" under Listen to hear the target, then build it with the first recipe.

Two further recipes follow: an optional probability variation of the ghost notes, and a separate, denser drum pattern at velocity 48 (the "Three sounds, one pocket" recording) that does not use ghost notes.

details.title: Complete example
details.text: Start at [Adding a Ghost Note](#pocket-rhythm). Follow its Before you start instructions and recipes in order. This is an independent project; save your course piece before trying it.

details.title: Comparison settings
details.text: The ghost-note comparison uses Oilcan 1. Every bar has four main attacks at velocity 90. Bars 3 and 4 each add one velocity-35 hit. The "Three sounds, one pocket" recording is an independent pattern at a constant velocity of 48. MIDI note mappings can differ on another instrument.

recipes.title: Make the recorded ghost-note comparison
recipes.text:
Starting point: an empty project with playback stopped and channel 1 selected. If Oilcan 1 is missing from the Device picker, install and enable `nb_oilcan` in SYSTEM > MODS; see [Norns Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b). The numbers 1–64 are step numbers across four bars: bar 1 is steps 1–16, bar 2 is 17–32, bar 3 is 33–48 and bar 4 is 49–64. For Masks and Pattern Trig, all 64 steps are visible together: row 4 is steps 1–16, row 5 is 17–32, row 6 is 33–48 and row 7 is 49–64; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. These screens do not page.


Setup (steps 1 to 3 prepare the instrument; do them once).

1. Assign Oilcan 1 to channel 1 and set its range to steps 1–64 (see Channel Length). Leave Rate at /1.

2. Set 90 BPM: open Song tasks, choose Tempo & feel, turn E3 to 90 and press K3.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Snap note masks to scale to Off, then return to Mosaic. MIDI 37 (C#1) is not in C major and would otherwise be snapped to a scale note. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then tap pattern slot (1,2) to assign pattern 1 to the channel.


Main hits (steps 4 to 7 build and audition the bar without ghost notes).

4. Add the main hits. Open Pattern Trig on pattern 1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 in each bar: bar 1 uses 1, 5, 9, 13; bar 2 uses 17, 21, 25, 29; bar 3 uses 33, 37, 41, 45; bar 4 uses 49, 53, 57, 61. Sixteen trigs are lit.

5. Open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). With no step held, select Note and set MIDI 36 (C1), select Vel and set 90, select Len and set ½. All sixteen hits now play MIDI 36 at velocity 90.

6. Select Note. Hold step 5 and turn E3 to MIDI 37 (C#1), then release. Do the same for steps 13, 21, 29, 37, 45, 53 and 61, so that the second and fourth beat of each bar play MIDI 37.

7. Press Play and listen to four bars of main hits only, then press Stop. You hear two timbres alternating on beats 1 to 4 of every bar.


Ghost notes (steps 8 to 10 add the quiet hit to bars 3 and 4).

8. Return to Pattern Trig and tap step 44 (step 12 of bar 3) and step 60 (step 12 of bar 4).

9. Open Masks and hold step 44. Select Note and turn E3 to MIDI 38 (D1), then select Vel and set 35, then release step 44. Repeat both edits on step 60: first Note 38, then Vel 35.

10. Press Play. Bars 1 and 2 are unchanged. In bars 3 and 4 you hear a quiet third timbre one step before each MIDI 37 accent. Press Stop.


Undo (step 11 returns to the main-only phrase).

11. Open Masks, hold step 44 or 60 and press K2 to remove the values you set, then remove its trig on Pattern Trig.

recipes.title: Optional probability variation
recipes.text:
Starting point: Finish the ghost-note comparison above with ghost trigs on steps 44 and 60. This is an optional, player-run probability exercise, not a reconstruction of the recording. At probability 50, each ghost onset may play or be skipped on each pass, so evaluate the range of outcomes over several loops instead of expecting a fixed recording.

**Set a dependable main beat.** Select channel 1 and open Channel tasks → Trig params. Turn E2 to a slot, press K2, turn E3 to Trig Probability, press K3. With no step held, set the channel default to 100. Check: every main hit remains eligible on every pass.

**Check both boundaries.** On the full Trig Params grid, hold step 44 at (12,6), set its probability to 0, and release. Hold step 60 at (12,7), set it to 0 the same way. Play: neither ghost note sounds in bars 3 or 4; the main hits continue. Stop. Set both ghost steps to 100 and play again: both ghost notes play on every pass, matching the fixed comparison. Stop.

**Try the optional variation.** Set steps 44 and 60 to 50 and play several loops. The musical result to listen for is a quiet pickup that appears on some passes and leaves space on others, while the main hits stay present. Which ghost hit appears can differ each loop; no particular pass or captured result is promised.

Restore the fixed comparison by setting both steps to 100, or remove a lock by holding its step and pressing K2. For a captured 0/100 probability example, see Trig Probability, “Turn chance into explicit rests.”

recipes.title: Separate fixed percussion example
recipes.text:
This is the "Three sounds, one pocket" recording. It is a different, denser four-bar drum pattern and does not use ghost notes. It teaches one idea: a third sound (MIDI 38) fills the gaps between the two accents. Every hit is at velocity 48, a constant quiet level chosen so you hear rhythm and timbre only, with no accent or quiet ghost hit. Starting point: the ghost-note comparison recipe's steps 1 to 3 (Oilcan 1 on channel 1, range 1–64, 90 BPM, Snap note masks to scale Off) and an empty channel.

The bar template, as step/MIDI note: 1/36, 4/38, 5/37, 7/38, 9/36, 12/38, 13/37 and 15/38.

Step:  1   4   5   7   9   12  13  15

Note:  36  38  37  38  36  38  37  38

1. Open Masks. With no step held, set Note to MIDI 36, Vel to 48 and Len to ½.

2. Enter the trigs. In bar 1, hold K1 and tap steps 1, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 13 and 15 to add eight trigs.

3. Edit the notes. Select Note and give steps 4, 7, 12 and 15 MIDI 38, and steps 5 and 13 MIDI 37, holding each step and turning E3. Steps 1 and 9 keep MIDI 36.

4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 in bars 2 to 4, adding 16 to each step number.

Play four bars. Listen for MIDI 36 on beats 1 and 3, MIDI 37 on beats 2 and 4, and the MIDI 38 hits filling the gaps between them. Unlike the ghost-note comparison, every hit has the same velocity, so nothing sounds accented or quiet. Listen to "Three sounds, one pocket" under Listen to compare.

title: Changing Harmony with Scale Slots
summary: Compare the same relative patterns under C major for two bars and D major for two bars.
prose:
Hear one pair of relative-note patterns in two keys. Doubledecker on channel 1 plays an upper phrase and Polyperc 1 on channel 2 plays a bass. For bars 1 and 2 the global scale is C major (scale slot 1); for bars 3 and 4 it is D major (scale slot 2). The patterns hold scale degrees, not fixed pitches, and the Note masks stay X (unset), so changing the applied scale moves every pitch while rhythm, velocity and length stay the same. Play "Changing Harmony with Scale Slots" under Listen to hear the target.

Settings: 90 BPM, Rate /1 (the default, one step is a sixteenth note) and a 16-step range that loops once per bar. The bass velocity is 60 and its notes last ½ step in this comparison. The "A bass with room above it" recording is a different example, in fixed notes in C major.

details.title: Complete example
details.text: Start at [Changing Harmony with Scale Slots](#tilting-harmony). Follow its Before you start instructions and recipes in order. This is an independent project; save your course piece before trying it.

details.title: Continue your course piece
details.text: For the phrase and bass you already made, open [Change harmony without changing the rhythm](#harmony-design/course). The independent comparison below uses Doubledecker for the upper phrase and Polyperc 1 for the bass, with two bars per key. Its voice assignments and section lengths differ from the course.

details.title: Pitch and output scope
details.text: This comparison uses relative pattern notes (scale degrees) with the Note masks left at X. A Note mask would replace the pattern note and fix the pitch, so no scale change could move it. Polyperc 1 is assigned once, to the bass. Numeric MIDI notes are used for expected results because the controls label octaves differently.

recipes.title: Make the relative-note scale comparison
recipes.text:
Starting point: an empty project with playback stopped. If Doubledecker or Polyperc 1 is missing from the Device picker, install and enable its corresponding `nb_doubledecker` or `nb_polyperc` mod in SYSTEM > MODS; see [Norns Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b). Part 1 builds the upper phrase on channel 1, part 2 builds the bass on channel 2, part 3 prepares the second key and part 4 performs the change. In the note page, the column is the step and the row is the degree: y=7 is degree 0 (I), y=6 is degree 1 (II) and y=3 is degree 4 (V).

Part 1: upper phrase

1. Set 90 BPM (Song tasks, Tempo & feel, E3, K3). Leave Rate at /1.

2. Open the Scale editor (4,8). Slot 1 at (1,3) is the applied slot. Check Root C and Scale Major on the Scale screen; if you change either, press K3 to save it.

3. Assign Doubledecker to channel 1. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1 and tap pattern slot (1,2) to assign pattern 1 to the channel. Open Pattern Trig, select pattern 1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13.

4. Open Pattern Note (tap Pattern (5,8) until Note is shown) and set the degrees: tap (1,7), (5,7) and (9,7) for degree 0, and (13,6) for degree 1. Set the channel range to steps 1-16.

5. Open Masks. Leave Note at X. Set Vel to 80 and Len to ½. Hold step 13 and set Vel to 50, then release. The phrase ends with a softer last note. Checkpoint: press Play and listen. In C major the upper phrase is MIDI 60, 60, 60, 62. Press Stop before building the bass channel.

Part 2: bass

6. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 2 and select pattern 2 for the channel. On pattern 2, tap steps 1 and 9 on Pattern Trig, then on Pattern Note tap (1,7) for degree 0 and (9,3) for degree 4. Set the range to steps 1-16 and the channel octave to -1 with (9,8).

7. Open Masks with channel 2 selected, leave Note at X, set Vel to 60 and Len ½. Checkpoint: press Play. The bass adds MIDI 48 on beat 1 and MIDI 55 on beat 3 under the upper phrase. Press Stop before preparing slot 2.

Part 3: prepare the second key

8. While stopped, open the Scale editor. Hold K1 and press slot 2 at (2,3) to select it for editing without applying it. On the Scale screen set Root to D and Scale to Major with E2 and E3, and press K3 to save the slot. Slot 1 stays applied, so playback is still C major.

Part 4: perform the change (choose one)

9a. Stopped: play two bars in C major and stop. Short-press slot 2 at (2,3) to apply D major and play two more bars.

9b. Live: while playing, short-press slot 2 at (2,3) at the end of bar 2.

Result check: in D major the upper phrase becomes MIDI 62, 62, 62, 64 and the bass becomes MIDI 50 and 57: the same rhythm moved up a whole tone. Short-press slot 1 at (1,3) to restore C major.

recipes.title: Separate fixed bass-and-chord example
recipes.text:
Goal and contrast: this example uses fixed Note masks, so its pitches do not move when the scale changes. It is the counterpart of the scale-slot comparison above, where the notes are relative degrees that move with the scale, and it shows how to layer quiet chords above a bass. It is the "A bass with room above it" recording and stays in C major.

Starting point: an empty project, 90 BPM, Rate /1, Snap note masks to scale at its default, and channels 1 and 2 with their range set to steps 1-16 (hold step 1 and tap step 16 on the channel page).

1. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1. Open Masks and set Note to MIDI 48, Vel to 48 and Len to ½.

2. Hold K1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. Hold step 9 and set Note to MIDI 55.

3. Assign Doubledecker to channel 2. Open Masks and set Note to MIDI 60, Vel to 32 and Len to 3 steps. Set Chd1 to 3rd and Chd2 to 5th.

4. Hold K1 and tap steps 1 and 9, then hold step 9 and set Note to MIDI 62.

5. Result check: press Play. The bass plays C2, C2, G2, C2 on beats 1 to 4; the chords sound C-E-G on beat 1 and D-F-A on beat 3. Chord velocity 32 is quieter than bass velocity 48. If the chord is missing, verify channel 2 uses a polyphonic device and Chd1=3rd and Chd2=5th.

title: Combining Four-Step and Three-Step Loops
summary: Use independent channel lengths to create a 12-step repeating relationship.
prose:
Run two channels at the same clock rate with different lengths: channel 1 loops a four-step phrase and channel 2 loops a three-step phrase. Both channels start together on step 1, drift apart, and meet again after 12 steps, the smallest number that both 4 and 3 divide into. At the default Rate /1 and 90 BPM, 12 steps last two seconds. Playback is continuous: each channel simply starts its own loop again when it reaches the end of its range.

1. On channel 1, assign a pattern with active steps 1–4. Using the default C-major scale, set relative pattern notes 0, 1, 2 and 3, which produce MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Set the velocities to 127, 117, 107 and 97 and each note length to one step. Set the range to steps 1–4 (hold step 1, tap step 4, release step 1).

2. On channel 2, assign the same pattern and set the range to steps 1–3.

3. Open channel 2 Masks. With no step held, set the channel defaults to Note MIDI 79, Vel 40 and Len ½.

4. Hold step 2 and set Note MIDI 81, Vel 60 and Len 1¼. Release the step. Channel 2 now repeats MIDI 79, 81, 79, independent of the four notes on channel 1.

5. Start playback. Both channels begin together. Compare their first steps again after 12 steps (about two seconds).

6. Stop playback before changing the arrangement.

Use separate MIDI routes for the two instruments. For internal sound, assign different supported players, for example Polyperc 1 for channel 1 and Doubledecker for channel 2. Song transitions and reset options can restart channels earlier than 12 steps; the second recipe shows how.

details.title: Complete example
details.text: Start at [Combining Four-Step and Three-Step Loops](#loops-that-meet). Follow its Before you start instructions and recipes in order. This is an independent project; save your course piece before trying it.

details.title: Example Scope
details.text: The four-against-three lesson below uses ranges 1–4 and 1–3. Its screen/grid demonstration and MIDI output show that small example. The separate recording Sixteen steps against twelve uses longer phrases; open its named extension recipe for the matching setup. Both illustrate loops meeting, but their note sequences and lengths differ.

recipes.title: Comparing the Loop Alignment
recipes.text:
Starting point: the numbered setup in Combining Four-Step and Three-Step Loops is complete and playback is stopped. Both channels run at the same rate. At 90 BPM and Rate /1 one step is a sixth of a second, so you can count 12 steps in two seconds.

1. Press Play and count steps. Channel 1 plays MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 and then repeats, so it completes three phrases in 12 steps. Channel 2 plays MIDI 79, 81, 79 and repeats, so it completes four phrases in the same 12 steps.

2. Listen at step 1: MIDI 60 and MIDI 79 sound together. This same pitch pair also occurs at step 9, so it is not unique. Count phrase starts: after step 1, the two loops next realign at step 13. On step 4, channel 1 plays MIDI 65 while channel 2 starts a new phrase with MIDI 79.

3. Listen at step 13, two seconds after step 1: MIDI 60 and MIDI 79 sound together again, and the pattern repeats every 12 steps. Press Stop when you have heard the alignment.

4. Optional extra check, unrelated to the alignment: with both channels playing, try a reversed range on channel 1. Hold step 4 as the start, press step 2 as the end and release both. The reversed range is rejected with a message, the ranges stay 1–4 and 1–3, and neither phrase changes timing.

recipes.title: Comparing Song Boundary Resets
recipes.text:
Starting point: the two looping channels above (channel 1 range 1–4, channel 2 range 1–3), with Song slot 1 holding them and playback stopped. Song mode is On by default, so the slots play in turn, and Reset on song seq change (PARAMS > MOSAIC) is On by default while Reset on pattern repeat is Off. This comparison hears how the first option changes both channels at a slot boundary.

1. Set slot 1 to ten steps before copying it. Open the Song Editor and tap slot 1 at (1,1). On the length fader, tap (2,7) to jump to 1, then tap (8,7) nine times to reach 10. This length belongs to the selected slot and applies to both its channels. Ten is not a multiple of 4 or 3, so each channel is part-way through its loop when the slot ends.

2. Copy the ten-step slot. Hold slot 1 at (1,1), tap slot 2 at (2,1), then release slot 1. Slot 2 inherits slot 1's patterns and length 10. Leave slot 3 empty and select slot 1 again: the two ten-step sections will play in turn.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and check that Reset on song seq change reads On. Play both slots. At the start of slot 2 both channels restart from step 1: channel 1 plays MIDI 60 and channel 2 plays MIDI 79. The 4-against-3 pattern starts again from the beginning in every slot. Press Stop.

4. Set Reset on song seq change to Off and play both slots again. Now neither channel restarts: at the start of slot 2 channel 1 continues with MIDI 64, the third note of its phrase (10 steps is two phrases and two steps), and channel 2 continues with MIDI 81, the second note of its phrase (10 steps is three phrases and one step). The two channels no longer meet at the slot boundary. Press Stop.

5. Set Reset on song seq change back to On to restore the default.

Use Off when you want the 12-step relationship to carry across slots without a restart; use On when each slot should begin with both loops on their first step.

recipes.title: Run two channels at different lengths
recipes.text:
Starting point: two channels with audible notes. Give each channel a voice (for example Oilcan 1 on channel 1 and Polyperc 1 on channel 2, or any two MIDI outputs) and set Note, Vel and Len on each channel's Masks page as in Make your first loop (a channel needs at least one audible note to be heard).

Enter the two patterns. Tap Pattern (5,8) for the Trig view. In pattern 1 tap steps (1,4), (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4): a drum pattern with trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. In pattern 2 tap steps (1,4), (3,4) and (4,4): a short figure with trigs on steps 1, 3 and 4.

1. Channel 1: tap (1,1) and assign pattern 1 at (1,2). Hold step 1 (grid (1,4)), tap step 16 ((16,4)), then release step 1. Steps 1-16 on row 4 are now brighter.

2. Channel 2: tap (2,1) and assign pattern 2 at (2,2). Hold step 1, tap step 5 ((5,4)), then release step 1. On this channel only steps 1-5 are brighter.

3. Tap Play at (1,8). The drum channel repeats every 16 steps (four hits per bar) and the figure repeats every 5 steps, so its three notes slide across the drum hits. Listen for the figure landing on a different drum beat each bar.

4. Keep listening until the start of drum bar 6. After 80 steps (five drum bars, sixteen figure passes) both channels start together again. 80 is the first step count that both 16 and 5 divide. Tap Play again to stop.

If the song moves to another song pattern, channels are reset together while Reset at Song Sequence Change (on by default) is enabled, so the 80-step cycle only completes while the same song pattern keeps playing. Use the Options page to change how channels of different length behave. The captured example [Play sixteen steps against five](#loops-that-meet/loops-sixteen-against-five) builds this setup and plays the 80 steps until both channels start together again. The captured example "Keep a valid range when a gesture is reversed" shows the range gesture and what happens when the end comes before the start.

recipes.title: Listening extension: sixteen steps against twelve
recipes.text:
Start from an empty independent project at 90 BPM and Rate /1, with Song mode off so the channel loops run continuously. This is the separate Sixteen steps against twelve recording.

1. Assign Oilcan 1 to channel 1 and set its range to steps 1–16. In Masks, set channel Vel 80 and Len 1/2. Add trigs on steps 1, 5, 9, 13 and 15. Set their Note masks to MIDI 36, 37, 36, 37 and 38 respectively.
2. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 2 and set its range to steps 1–12. In Masks, set channel Vel 60 and Len 1/2. Add trigs on steps 1, 4, 7 and 10. Set their Note masks to MIDI 48, 55, 52 and 55 respectively. Keep Snap note masks to scale Off so the drum note numbers stay unchanged.
3. Press Play. The loops meet every forty-eight steps: listen for the bass phrase landing differently against the drums in bars 2 and 3, then both returning to their first step at the beginning of bar 4.
4. Stop after four bars to match the recording. The bass ends four steps into its next twelve-step loop. This setup has different notes, sounds and loop lengths from the four-against-three lesson; keep the projects separate.
